The petitions in MVC No.5376/2019 and MVC No.5377/2019 are filed by the petitioner Somasundharam M., and Deen Dayalan M., respectively, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act ('M.V.Act' for short), praying for judgment and award granting compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
with interest at 18% p.a., from the date of petition till payment regarding the injuries sustained by them the road traffic accident.
MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 2.

The contention of the petitioner in MVC No.5376/2019 is that on 30.04.2019, at about 12.40 pm.,
the petitioner was travelling as pillion rider on Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA.53/EC.6785 along with his brother from Kalkere towards Rampur.
At that time, the Lorry bearing registration No.KA.50/7967 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the Motor Cycle from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries such as injuries on right leg, foot and fingers and other grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Koshis Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment.
Thereafter, he took treatment at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru.
As on the date of filing of this petition, he was still under treatment and spent Rs.10,000/- for medical treatment, conveyance etc.
Due to the injuries MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disability.
3. As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 26 years and he was hale and healthy.
He was working as Musician (Drum Player) and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot earn and suffered loss of earning.
He has to suffer the constant pain and discomfort throughout his life and thereby, he has suffered loss of income.
The accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry No.KA.50/6785 by its driver.
The respondents are the owners of the said Lorry.
Hence, the petitioner in MVC No.5376/2019 has prayed for allowing the petition.
4. The petitioner in MVC No.5377/2019 is Deen Dayalan M.
As per his contention, at the time of accident, he was riding the Motorcycle No.KA.53/EC.6785 along with his brother as pillion MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 rider.

As discussed herein above, the petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry by its driver and in the accident the petitioners suffered injuries.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Lorry, is liable to pay compensation, as determined above in the respective cases, to the petitioners and both the petitions as against the respondent No.2 are liable to be dismissed.

34. Point No.4:

In the result, therefore, I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER MVC No.5376/2019

The petition in MVC No.5376/2019 filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs against the respondent No.1 only and dismissed against the respondent No.2.

The petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.52,000/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount and he shall deposit the compensation amount with interest thereon within 2 months from the date of award.
On deposit, as the amount of compensation awarded is meager, entire compensation amount with accrued interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.

The petition in MVC No.5377/2019 filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs against the respondent No.1 only and dismissed against the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,32,100/- with interest at 6% per annum on MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 Rs.1,17,100/- only, from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and he shall deposit the compensation amount with interest thereon within 2 months from the date of award.
On deposit, as the amount of compensation awarded is meager, entire compensation amount with accrued interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in both the petitions.
The award shall be drawn  accordingly.

 Judgment
The petitions in MVC No.5376/2019 and MVC No.5377/2019 are filed by the petitioner Somasundharam M., and Deen Dayalan M., respectively, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act ('M.V.Act' for short), praying for judgment and award granting compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
with interest at 18% p.a., from the date of petition till payment regarding the injuries sustained by them the road traffic accident.
MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 2.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries such as injuries on right leg, foot and fingers and other grievous injuries all over the body.
Due to the injuries MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disability.
3. As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 26 years and he was hale and healthy.
He was working as Musician (Drum Player) and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot earn and suffered loss of earning.
He has to suffer the constant pain and discomfort throughout his life and thereby, he has suffered loss of income.
The accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry No.KA.50/6785 by its driver.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries such as fracture shaft humerus left, fracture of 1st metacarpal and other grievous injuries all over the body.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disability.
He was working as Musician (Drum Player) and earning MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 Rs.20,000/-
p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot earn and suffered loss of earning.
He has to suffer the constant pain and discomfort throughout his life and thereby, he has suffered loss of income.
The accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry No.KA.50/6785 by its driver.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Now the points that arise for my determination are:
 1) Whether the petitioner in MVC  No.5376/2019 proves that on 30.04.2019, at about 12.40 pm., near K. Channasandra Road in front of Tiles MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 Stores, he being the pillion rider of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA.53/EC.6785, met with the accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA.50/7957 by its driver and he suffered injuries in the accident as averred in the petition?
Whether the petitioner in MVC No.5377/2019 proves that on 30.04.2019, at about 12.40 pm., near K. Channasandra Road in front of Tiles Stores, he being the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA.53 /EC.6785, met with the accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA.50/ 7957 by its driver and he suffered injuries in the accident as averred in the petition?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation and if so, what amount and from whom?
4) What order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In spite of appearance, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to contest the MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 petition.
Therefore, the evidence on record would show that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries and consequently, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head Pain and Agony.
In the circumstances of the case, an amount of Rs.20,000/- would be proper and reasonable compensation payable to the petitioner under the head Pain and Agony.
22. Moreover, the petitioner was treated as an outpatient in two hospitals.
Hence, during the period of treatment and also thereafter at the time of follow-up treatment, the petitioner would have spent some amount towards his conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Moreover, the petitioner suffered fracture of 2nd and 4th Metatarsal bone.
The MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 said fracture injury would not cause any inconvenience to the petitioner for doing his work as Musician (Drum Player).
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under the head loss of income due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
However, the petitioner suffered fracture of 2nd and 4th metatarsal bone and he was treated as outpatient in two hospital ie., Koshys Hospital and Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Benglauru.
Moreover, considering the nature of injury i.e., fracture of left humerus suffered by the petitioner in the accident MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 and the period of 7 days as inpatient, the petitioner would require some amount towards attendant charges during the period of inpatient, conveyance expenses, attendant charges and other incidental expenses after the discharge from the hospital.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards expenses for future medical treatment.
It is not the case of the respondent No.1 that the said Lorry was insured at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Lorry, is liable to pay compensation, as determined above in the respective cases, to the petitioners and both the petitions as against the respondent No.2 are liable to be dismissed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.20,000/- is awarded in favour of the petitioner under the head pain and agony.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,914/- towards medical expenses incurred for his treatment.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,914/- under the head expenses towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment and other expenses.
Hence, the compensation of Rs.17,000/- is granted in favour of the petitioner under the head expenses MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment and other expenses.
24. In view of the reasons mentioned herein above, the petitioner is entitled to the compensation under different heads as the following:
MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 Sl. No. Particulars Amount in Rs.
 1) Pain and agony 20,000.00  2) Medical Expenses 17000.00  including conveyance,
 nourishment and other  charges
3 ) Loss of amenities 15,000.00
In the circumstances, considering the nature of injury and the treatment already taken by MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 the petitioner, a notional amount of Rs.15,000/- is hereby allowed as compensation for the expenses towards future medical treatment, which shall not carry any interest.
Therefore, a notional compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of loss of amenities.
32. In view of the reasons mentioned herein above, the petitioner is entitled to the compensation under different heads as the following:
Sl. No. Particulars Amount in Rs.
34. Point No.4:
From the discussion made herein above, it is clear that the above petitions deserve to be allowed in part against the respondent No.1 and the same are liable to be MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 dismissed against the respondent No.2.
In the result, therefore, I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER MVC No.5376/2019
The petition in MVC No.5376/2019 filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs against the respondent No.1 only and dismissed against the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.52,000/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount and he shall deposit the compensation amount with interest thereon within 2 months from the date of award.
On deposit, as the amount of compensation awarded is meager, entire compensation amount with accrued interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
MVC No.5377/2019
The petition in MVC No.5377/2019 filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs against the respondent No.1 only and dismissed against the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,32,100/- with interest at 6% per annum on MVC No.5376/2019 c/w.5377/2019 Rs.1,17,100/- only, from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and he shall deposit the compensation amount with interest thereon within 2 months from the date of award.
On deposit, as the amount of compensation awarded is meager, entire compensation amount with accrued interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in both the petitions.
The award shall be drawn  accordingly.
